plan: Given the common knowledge of rationality, the optimal bidding strategy converges towards bidding your true value minus a small amount. This is because bidding too high risks overpaying, while bidding too low risks losing the item even when it's worth more than the bid. Since this is round 1 and there is no previous history, I will bid slightly below my value to attempt to win at a reasonable price. I will bid $24.5.

Since this is a single-round auction with rational bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid slightly above the expected value of the second-highest bid. Given the values are between $0 and $49, a conservative estimate for the second-highest bid is around half of my value. I will bid slightly above that to increase my chances of winning without overpaying. My value is $18, so I'll bid $10.5.

Given the common knowledge of rationality and a single round, the optimal bidding strategy converges to bidding your true value minus a small increment. This is because any bid above your value risks overpaying, and any bid below risks losing the item when it's worth more to you than the bid. Since bids are in $0.1 increments, I will bid $30.90.
